Maybe you've experienced tension with friends who lost their jobs or found themselves deep in debt. Or perhaps you've been in one of those situations yourself. From lifestyles to special events (and even the treacherous waters of personal loans), what are your tips for managing friendships when money issues come up?

Got your own idea for a discussion? Post a thread! /v/relationships welcomes both relationship advice and general discussion questions.
Discussion: Is there a way to avoid awkwardness between friends who are in very different financial situations?

If a friend is in need and I have the means, I'll loan the money, but they'll need to provide a good reason if it's not pocket money. I won't berate them for not paying back, and if I know it's not their fault I won't care at all. If I don't get paid back because of poor money management, I won't get mad but I won't loan more either (though I might buy things for them, but the initiative would be mine). If I don't get paid back, with no reason, I'll stop seeking that friend. Usually after weeks or months, I'll remind whoever owns me to pay back in a friendly manner, but I'll drop the subject after 2-3 times.

However, I've had multiple cases where I have loaned friends during emergencies, with the means to pay back, and they haven't. I stopped seeking these friends; my reasoning is that they are the kind of person that like to take and not give; who knows what they do to other people, and if they are only around me to squeeze resources out of me.

I've also had the case of a friend where I've loaned money, he's still going through a rough patch, asked for more money and I've refused given that he didn't pay back; he didn't push me away, but he stopped seeking me. It might be important to know that I've known him for many years and I know his main interest in me is not money.

I've also had friends to whom I've loaned money multiple times, and they have paid back on time every time, without me even having to remind them.

I've read AMAs on reddit from rich people, the kind of people that can afford to fly on a private plane. It seems that for starters, they try to only have friends within the same economic level just because it's easier, but when they do get friends who are not wealthy, it will take months for their friends to know they have money, and by then they will make these friends go through multiple test to ensure that they are not the kind of person that will react unfavorably to money. Even then, it happens sometimes, and regular or close contact will stop, though it doesn't always means the friendship will be cut off completely.

I make more money than some of my friends and less than others. If I'm golfing with my buddy who makes twice as much as me, he tends to buy the beer, which I in turn to do for my less fortunate friends. This is not to say he's always buying me shit, I get rounds in too, however, if someone were to break it all down on paper over the years, he's most likely spent more money. On the other hand, he did sleep on my couch for a year for free when we were younger because he had some problems at home. This isn't some form of repayment, it's just an example of friends doing something nice for each other without counting pennies or expecting reimbursement.

To summarize, if you're actually friends, you'll do nice things for each other without keeping a tally. If you're concerned about going places some friends can't afford, don't invite them. Personally I would suggest that in the long run you'll be happier if you stop pinching pennies.

Doing something nice for someone and not looking for anything in return is one of lifes little pleasures that can pay unexpected dividends sometime down the road.

A lot of people may take a break from a substance (such as alcohol or caffeine) to prove they do not have an addiction. The issue is they know it is a predetermined interval of time and once it is up they can binge hardcore once again. This is why diets, breaks from drinking, etc. don't tend to work. I had an idea for if you don't want to stop using something forever but prove it doesn't have power over you: enter random number generators.

So let us use alcohol as an example. Instead of taking a month long break of something like that, you go about your normal day, but you have a random number generator. Any time you would normally drink you generate a number, lets say 1-9. If that number is odd, you don't drink, no excuse, no rerolls, etc. If the number is even, you may proceed as normal. You may only check once per day and the check lasts 24 hours. Use something like random.org or generate the numbers, and you must abide by whatever the number dictates. If you are able to follow this, you don't have a problem, but if you break the rule, even once, it proves you are not in control. The reason I think this is superior to typical breaks is the lack of predictability. You could get a really bad run of luck and have to not have it for a while, or the bad luck could strike at a time where you are really having a rough time emotionally or otherwise. If you are able to follow the tyranny of entropy then you have the will power, if not then any break you could have taken has proven to be a lie.

Obviously if you have a problem with something then complete cessation would be a better route, but I think this is an interesting litmus test for the mathematically and substance inclined. Thoughts?

I've been doing something conceptually similar, except instead of rolling to drink/etc, I've been rolling on how to spend my time to avoid procrastinating. I think it's been generally successful for me in that although I'm not actually spending more time productively, I've managed to finish things earlier than before.

My system was this, keeping in mind I'm a student: Every day was broken up into four two-hour blocks loosely, and there are five days in a week (all the other time is automatically allocated to doing whatever I want and classes). This makes 20 time blocks per week.

On the nth time block, roll 1d20 and apply the following:

  • 1: Goof off after making any amount of progress on my next task. For an assignment this would be as simple as downloading the assignment's PDF, if I needed groceries then all I'd need to do is find my wallet so I won't have to look for it later when I'm going out for groceries, etc.
  • 2 - n: Work on whatever task had priority, whether it be going out to get groceries or studying or whatever else, tasks were prioritized pretty much however I wanted; generally based on when they needed to be completed by.
  • Anything else: Do whatever I want.

I also allowed myself to save "whatever I want" time blocks for later, ie if I wanted to go to a friend's place after dinner, I can defer a "whatever I want" time block that I rolled right now until then and roll again.
